column1: # Every architecture the OpenWrt buildbot publishes, with a target that builds
# it and the emulator to run it under.
# Columns: arch, target, qemu program, cpu model.
# The cpu model is always named, never left to the emulator's default. The
# default 32-bit PowerPC model does not implement isel, and musl for
# powerpc_8548 (CPU_TYPE 8548, the e500v2 core in parts such as the P1010) holds
# 63 of them, so the C library faults with an illegal instruction before
# reaching main, whatever the package holds. That reads exactly like a package
# failure and is not one. Naming the model removes the guesswork.
# Each model here was checked by running that target's own musl loader under it.
# Where the exact CPU is absent from qemu-user, the closest superset is used, on
# the reasoning that too weak a model invents failures while too rich a model
# hides them and skews runtime feature detection:
#   arm_cortex-a5_vfpv4   cortex-a7   no cortex-a5 in qemu-user
#   arm_xscale            arm926      no xscale or pxa model
#   i386_pentium-mmx      pentium2    closest with MMX and no SSE
#   i386_pentium4         n270        no pentium4; pentium3 lacks SSE2
# arm_fa526 is build-only, and the reason is the emulator rather than the
# package. That target compiles to plain ARMv4, which has no bx and so cannot
# enter Thumb code: the binary holds no bx or blx at all, where the ARMv5 build
# of the same package holds 133. qemu-user always maps a Thumb vdso, so the call
# to __vdso_gettimeofday runs Thumb bytes in ARM state and branches into the
# weeds. Real hardware never meets this, because the Linux ARM vdso needs ARMv7
# and a gemini kernel supplies none, leaving musl on plain syscalls. The
# currently shipped package fails identically, so it is not a change here, and
# qemu-user offers no way to withhold the vdso. Naming a v7 model would hide
# genuine mismatches, so the packet test is skipped and the build still runs.
# riscv64_riscv64 is the name the release branches use for riscv64_generic, and
# no current target produces mips_4kec, so neither appears here.
